issues.description: The template's make_y_state function is missing the depolarization probability parameter `p` required by the problem specification. The problem statement and the solution both define make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None, but the template declares make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int) -> None. This prevents students from implementing the prescribed noisy |Y> state preparation (which must accept a noise parameter p) and is inconsistent with the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template function signature to include the depolarization parameter: def make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None. Update any docstring and usages in the template accordingly so students can implement the noisy |Y> preparation as specified.

issues.description: The function make_y_state is specified in the problem statement and implemented in the solution to accept a depolarization parameter p (signature: make_y_state(circ, q, p)), but the template stub defines make_y_state without the p parameter (signature: make_y_state(circ, q)). This mismatch in the function signature prevents students from matching the required API and will cause confusion and test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template's make_y_state function signature to include the depolarization parameter p (make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None) and adjust the docstring accordingly so it matches the problem statement and the solution implementation.
